_help: Your prompt library. 'prompts' are the one-click actions on selected text (and figures/tables: scope 'area'); placeholders {{text}} (the selection), {{context}} (the paragraph around it), {{title}}, {{authors}}, {{year}}. 'summaries' are the templates for paper summaries; placeholders {{interests}}, {{title}}, {{journal}}, {{doi}}. Edit here or in Settings → Prompts.

prompts.name: Explain in plain words
Define the term
Why does this matter?
Hidden assumptions
Turn into a research question
Translate to Portuguese
prompts.prompt:
Translate the selected text into European Portuguese, keeping technical terms accurate. Output only the translation.

{{text}}

prompts.name: Explain this figure or table
prompts.prompt: Explain the attached figure or table from the paper "{{title}}": what it shows, how to read it (axes, columns, units), the main takeaway, and any caveat visible in it. If it is a table, list the key numbers.

summaries.name: IS brief (default)
summaries.prompt:
Read this paper in full and write a markdown summary for an IS researcher
whose interests are: {{interests}}.

Use exactly this structure:

# {{title}}
**Authors**: ... | **Journal**: {{journal}} | **Year**: ... | **DOI**: {{doi}}
**Matched interests**: ...
## TL;DR
2-3 sentences.
## Research question & contribution
## Method
Data, setting, identification/design, sample size.
## Key findings
- one bullet per finding, with effect sizes where reported
## Implications
For research and for practice.
## Limitations & open questions
## Relevance to your interests
1-2 lines tying it to the matched interests.

Output only the markdown.

summaries.name: Theory & contribution
summaries.prompt:
Read this paper in full and write a markdown note on its theory and contribution for an IS researcher with interests in: {{interests}}.

# {{title}}
## Theoretical lens
Which theories, and how they are used (extended, tested, challenged).
## Constructs and propositions
Key constructs with definitions; hypotheses or propositions and whether they were supported.
## Contribution
What is new relative to prior work, and to whom it matters.
## Boundary conditions
Where the argument should and should not hold.
## How I could use it
Three concrete ways this could feed my own research.

Output only the markdown.

summaries.name: Methods & data
summaries.prompt:
Read this paper in full and write a markdown replication brief.

# {{title}}
## Design
Research design and identification strategy.
## Data
Source, period, unit of analysis, sample size and filters.
## Measures
Key variables, how they are built, scales or models used.
## Estimation
Model specifications, controls, robustness checks.
## Threats to validity
What a sceptical reviewer would press on.
## What I would need to replicate
Data access, code, tools.

Output only the markdown.

summaries.name: 5-line TL;DR
summaries.prompt: Read this paper and write exactly five bullet points, each one sentence: (1) the question, (2) the method and data, (3) the main finding, (4) the contribution, (5) the main limitation. Title: {{title}}. Output only the five bullets.
